Filed on the service board 2026-09-24: the classifier LLM budget cannot fit the webhook guard. One ModelSettings(timeout=30) object is handed to both legs and the OpenRouter loop retries 3 models, so the worst case is 30 + 3x30 = 120 s against a 55 s webhook and Telegram's 60 s ceiling - the fallback can never finish. Second half: handle_update awaited the update under asyncio.wait_for, so the deadline CANCELLED the classification and nothing persisted the verdict, so a redelivery re-entered the same race from zero. Measured 15.1x the baseline rate: 7 distinct timeout events in 1.24 h against 45 in 120 h.

Taken by the ai-antispam HQ lane and implemented in this lane's plan (Classifier timeout budget and verdict persistence). Fix shipped in 48dc509 on both remotes. The post-deploy 72 h log verification, which is the close condition, is dispatched to the Bot lane.

Filed on the service board 2026-09-24: the OpenRouter fallback tier was effectively dead and admin notifications were refused as too long. (1) per_attempt is derived as (budget-gateway)/len(models) = (45-18)/3 = 9.0s while the models need 3-27s; measured over 12:16-18:16Z: 265 classifications, 235 gateway ok / 30 timeouts, fallback rescued 3/30 (10.0%), 27 messages (10.2%) unmoderated, 85 OpenRouter attempts failed and 0 succeeded. One configured model (lightning:free) measured 45-56s against a 45s total budget. (2) format_admin_notification_message embedded the user text unbounded; live spam text reaches 3665 chars and the assembled message hit 4339 against Telegram's 4096, so the API refused it and the admin never learned spam was caught.
